utterances.text: Yes, exactly, but witness, my question is that given the scale of the map that you have in front of you and the position of the Holiday Inn hotel, could you perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was what was the distance between Tito barracks and the Holiday Inn. By making reference to the scale of the map, you are introducing new elements. Could I ask you, you said that it was approximately one kilometre --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at least a kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us on the basis of what you tell us this, is that because you walk that distance or you drove that distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I drove that distance down this road here past Marsal Tito, okay, to the Presidency which is just here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the question was about the distance between the Holiday Inn and the Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. It would probably -- based on this here, it would be 1.8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please point at this map where the Holiday Inn Is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the witness has already done that. The witness was asked where the Holiday Inn and the building alongside that were. We've marked that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I just try to -- could you please indicate where the Holiday Inn Is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure it's in this area here. I've never been to the Holiday Inn, okay. I've only -- I've been very close to the Holiday Inn but I've never been into it or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you locate the Holiday Inn in what I just called the old city, the area you were pointing at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very close to it, yes, and the road that the photo was taken from that we've all been looking at is this road here and it -- and it's pointing it's facing north and the Holiday Inn is just in this area here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness now points at a spot just north of what is indicated on the map as Marsala Tita especially the area just next to the Marsala Tita north of Mrakusa where approximately a triangular green spot is on the map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you use the pointer to point to the map or indicate the direction of fire in relation to the attack that we mentioned a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That's the direction of fire from the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the tank attacking but the attack that you yourself said came from the east. Could you indicate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, the witness points to an area that is parallel to the road called Marsal Tito Road in the direction of the east. Thank you very much. Could you please have a look at the extreme eastern part of this map? Could you have a look at that area and I hope that we'll be able to see the far eastern part of this map. With the assistance of the usher, we need to move the map up a bit. Thank you. Could you use a black felt-tip to draw an arrow and to show in which direction -- to show where the Serbian positions were located in the east, use an arrow to do so. Thank you. And tell us, please, very roughly, how many kilometres were these positions from the extreme part of the map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: At least another two kilometres off the map, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the witness has been quite clear. I'd like to move on to another subject and could we show the very first part of the video, it's a scene that was filmed at night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I'm -- I would like to see the sequence which you asked so many questions again, not necessarily immediately, that's one. But I've still got no idea what video this is when I compare the voice of this witness. He's not the one who's speaking so I wonder what we are looking at? Are we looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We received a certain number of video documents from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... From what it is and you perhaps ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll check that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I think you are in a position to tell us whether you can recognise the images that you saw a minute ago as images that are part of the material that you provided us with; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the part that we just had a look at, could you tell us what the origin of that sequence is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It's from a BBC recording of events in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, any other questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you record it yourself, did you see it on television and had a video recorder? How does it -- how did it come to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was -- I had a number of military observers in Sarajevo. One of them happened to be a New Zealander and he went to the TV station which was right next door to the PTT building and he obtained all these videotapes for me. He obtained them from their unedited raw footage of the actual war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say BBC, was that a BBC office or were there more broadcasting companies? How do you know that this was the BBC sequence? I'm just trying to find out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because if you actually look at the videotape you will actually see BBC on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's perhaps the reason why we have to look again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it actually gives you the countdown, ten, nine, one and then it shows the actual sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I haven't seen any of the countdown but perhaps we'll start.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that Mr. Ierace could confirm that on occasion we had 15, 14, 13, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It's a BBC sequence then of course it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I've seen I think about two and a half hours of BBC footage on these tapes. The date is incorrect. Most of them carry the date the 16th of June 1992, that's clearly incorrect. The time is repeated as well, that's probably incorrect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I accept that all of the footage I saw was taken in 1992 and perhaps the witness could assist us with his recollection as to some events that we're about to see - not this one in particular - occurred. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I have a last question, you copied it from your UNMO who got it for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he copied it for me and in fact the videotapes, if you want to have a look at them, you'll find out that they -- a number of them have got inscribed on them a -- that they are actually from the Defence film library in New Zealand, they've actually got numbers on them, actually burnt into the actual cassette tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it copied for you later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was copied for me later and that's why the Prosecutor said here well they all show actually the 11th of June but what happened was they copied this material in one session and they all show the same date on the actual footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you got a copy which was prepared in -- not in Sarajevo but later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was prepared in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The copy was prepared in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was actually prepared in the TV station next door to the PTT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So he did not only obtain his copy but he also there copied a version for you or.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea if he actually took his own copy but this is a copy that he took for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We'll have a look at this sequence a little later but perhaps we could have a look at the first sequence if the technical booth is ready. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might we just clarify which tape that was on, it's a matter of disclosure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's a good question. It's one of the four tapes that you were provided with but I can't tell you which one, Mr. Ierace. We worked on this very late in the night without calling you, I know, but I can't tell you which cassette we used. It was a patchwork but it's among the material that you have. It's either the one that you saw this morning or the one that you saw yesterday but I don't know. I would have to review the four tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... There are six or seven lines to say what I understand to be I can't tell you immediately, I'll check it at short notice but it certainly is in the material we provided to you. That would be one line and a half, approximately, which would ... You checked that it was one line and a half, I see. I think that -- let's try to spend our time as efficiently as possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise yourself at the end of this tape?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that they could destroy the entire city if they wanted to, who were you referring to when you said "they"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I was referring to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with regard to the first part of this sequence, we saw an attack carried out at night. My question is as follows: Did such attacks -- did such night-time attacks occur frequently?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who started these attacks, which side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: We had a observation post set up on top of the PTT and we also had other observation posts set up. The attacks normally started on the inside and then they were retaliated by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, the Serbian reaction, was it normal, was it abnormal from a military point of view, was it understandable?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It was probably disproportionate to what was actually going out. What was coming in from the Serbs was certainly a lot heavier but they had more weapons and therefore, where one or two rounds went out then ten rounds came in. It was just a fact of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If we put aside the issue of the proportionality of the response, was the response a legitimate one according to your professional experience or was it not a legitimate one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: When you get fired at you normally fire back, so yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the middle of this scene that we had a look at a minute ago, we could see a radar. If you know anything about this, what could you tell us about this radar, what was its purpose and secondly, what did it allow you, one, to do, and to know and thirdly what happened to it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Okay. The radar was there, the two of them were actually brought in. They're from, obviously, the Ukraine, that was on the videotape. They were there to actually locate and give indications to the UN where fire was coming from, where it was going to. They are specifically radars for mortar and artillery, not for high velocity weapons, they had a technical function to do that. The radar was -- that we actually saw on the videotape was located close to Papa 7, I can show you on the map, if you want me to, and one of the radars was damaged when it first arrived at Sarajevo airport and it was never functional again, it was just moved away so there was only one radar. That radar was basically put out of action by fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether an investigation was launched to determine the source of fire which rendered this radar useless, put it out of service?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: An investigation was launched and it was determined that the -- because it was poorly located, which had nothing to do with me, but it was a technical problem that happened, because it was poorly located, it was sitting on the top of a ridge line, as I say, it was close to Papa 7 and it was put out of action by -- we can only assume, and that's the conclusion that we came to, it was put out of action by Serb fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have a look at the second part of this tape, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the transcript, usually we have a transcript from videotapes. I do understand that it could not yet have been prepared. We do not have the spoken text of the video now in our transcript. May I take it that if one of these sequences is tendered into evidence that sooner or later a transcript of the text will be provided as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we'll do that gladly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have not seen any number yet either so the way, if this material is tendered, should be such that there could be no confusion whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for that reason, it may be appropriate that we see each of the four sequences, whether it's the Prosecution or Defence playing them, because if we don't see the transcript for some days, it's going to be very difficult to remember back as to where the part played commenced and where it finished if it isn't the full segment. The segments range from two minutes to three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand but perhaps -- well, the first segment will be played again as far as I understand. The second one -- for the time being, I ask the parties to work hard in writing down any relevant part of the -- trying to catch the commentary, the voice so that we can work with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I might also observe at this stage that we haven't been told by the Defence which documents they intend to tender, which particular video segments they intend to tender. A number of videotapes and documents have been disclosed to us, that's one of the difficulties I have at the moment. And because there are so many segments on each of these tapes, it is difficult to work out what's being disclosed, what hasn't, what's to be tendered and then locating it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must say that yesterday in order to assist the Prosecution, I provided them with a piece of paper on which we mentioned the places that we thought -- where we thought we would find interesting things. That's what I was able to do I wasn't able to do more than that and by the way, if there is one side that is handicapped by the lack of the English transcript, it's the Defence. It's certainly not the Prosecution, but we are going to do everything that we can in order to carry this out but I can say that there are going to be nine sequences which will be different and it's easy to recognise them on the basis of their differences. There are night-time scenes, there are daytime scenes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll speed up. May I do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please then proceed and if during the break you could give further information to the Prosecution on what parts you intend to play and to tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't want to waste time but Mr. Piletta-Zanin is correct he did give me some information last night. I am grateful for that. I found that I was unable to locate the particular segments. I'm simply saying that I'm not being overly critical of my friend but there are problems and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have not solved them yet and the parties are urged to do whatever they can to accommodate the other party and let's now proceed as indicated before the Prosecution if the Prosecution would need extra time to prepare for cross-examination they can ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If we could begin the segments with the BBC black and white part and that will make the transcript more accurate ultimately, in terms of what's being shown

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President we're going to carry on in order but we will start from the second sequence in order to save time. Second sequence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we commence, this is the difficulty. How can we remember in a week's time exactly where this segment commenced in terms of transcript? Is it not better to commence it with the BBC black and white.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course there always is an opportunity to look back at the composite video picture of this so if needed, we could trace it but -- so that is possible although it would take a lot of time but I'd prefer now to start and if -- I have some hesitation to ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin to indicate what he will see because he might ask the witness afterwards what he has seen. And that's not a proper way of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To help the Prosecution, I can say that the next sequence, as far as I can remember, should start with the image of a young man carrying a gun and bearing a lily on his chest. I think that's what I can remember

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's before that, just before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, -- could we stop --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Spoken on the second was: "It was a tank, a tank". That's perhaps identifies the sequences and it started with: "This morning the Bosnian." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could we fix on the image at the place where we saw the last image, what can we see here? What can you see here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That's an assault rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is holding it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It's being held by a Muslim fighter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps tell us the sex of the person holding the rifle?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That's a male.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you whether you know whether there were any women who fought in the army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes -- on what side, on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of duties could they perform, what sort of posts could they hold?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: They had snipers there. They had female snipers. It's on the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we carry on and view the continuation of the cassette?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to stop here, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to this sequence that we just saw, I have two questions, the first question is that we heard the soldier say that Muslims soldiers were good fighters and that they could go anywhere. What can you comment in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Numerically, I believe, in terms of manpower, the Presidency forces had more manpower. In terms of heavy weapons, the Serbs had more heavy weapons and that's all I can really comment upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But particularly this person who was speaking said that he could go anywhere, pass through anything. What can you say about the qualities of infantry soldiers, Muslim infantry soldiers to infiltrate themselves anywhere, what can you comment regarding this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: The Presidency forces were being reinforced from outside Sarajevo and there may have been a lot of media hype about a siege but we found, on Serb positions, mortar tail fins which had Arabic writing on them and they came from outside Sarajevo and they were being reinforced not only with ammunition and food but also soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, at the end of this sequence, we saw these men, three men wearing yellow and blue, but they seemed to be civilians who were bearing weapons and they seemed to be relatively young men. What can you tell us about the use by the Muslim army of young men who were below the legal age of 18?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: There were a lot of young men who were fighting for the Muslims or Presidency. They usually distinguished themselves by having a bandanna around their head or a sweatband, what I would call a sweatband around their head and it was a different colours for different companies or platoons, whatever, to differentiate who they were from. They were mostly dressed in civilian clothing because they just didn't have uniforms but they were fighters nonetheless and some were very young.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have a look at the following sequence, technical booth, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then immediately if we can have the following sequence, the fourth sequence to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just stop for one second. This section just started with "some mortar and small arms fire," that was the text spoken and it ended with the words "... For most of the day," I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The following sequence, BBC news, 11th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The sequence is finished -- ends with the word "however".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This last section started: "It was the heaviest fighting since the airlift." That's what is in my recollection. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Yes, I said this was BBC news 2037 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, with these two sequences that we just saw, and there was talk of an area called Dobrinja, your recollection, could you please tell us to what Dobrinja corresponds and which one of the two sides was there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Dobrinja was held by the Presidency side and directly next to it was Nedzarici. Both of the two suburbs were adjacent to the airport and at the other end of Dobrinja was Lukavica which was held by the Serb side. So it basically went a Serb, Muslim, Serb in Nedzarici and then you've got the Stup, and Stup was Croat. And then to the west was Ilidza which was a Serb-held suburb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about the east side and could you please tell us to which cardinal point in relation to the airport is the area of Dobrinja located, the south or north of the airport?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Can I have the map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I can rephrase my question in order to save time. On the other side of Dobrinja, on the other side of the airport, is there a settlement and which one is it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It's Butmir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, there was talk of exchange of fire in these two sequences, video sequences. Can you tell us, according to your recollection, since we are talking about the area of Dobrinja, between which location and which location, that is locations and locations was there this exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Dobrinja was firing at Nedzarici and Nedzarici were firing back and we had Lukavica firing at Dobrinja as well and we also had Butmir firing directly across the airport which was not good, and then Butmir were firing at Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Butmir was firing directly across the airport and this wasn't good can you tell us why was it this -- why was this not good?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Well, I mean we were trying to help everyone, I mean, all sides in Sarajevo and yet we had all these bullets and shells which were, I mean they were hangars there for planes, we had food in there, we had we had all sorts of things, equipment and so on and we had Butmir was firing directly across the airport into Nedzarici, it was all the headquarters for one of the battalions and so I mean that wasn't good either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, earlier, you spoke in response to a question about women, you said that there were women snipers. What can you briefly, briefly tell us about snipers and women snipers on the side of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Well, there is -- I mean on one of the videotapes, it will show quite clearly that there is -- there was one very famous, infamous, woman sniper for the Muslim forces who was firing on a daily basis against the Serbian forces. I only recall there being one part of the videotape which shows that one particular woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But what can you tell us, not about a particular video but in general, witness, what can you tell us about the situation in relation to both armies, but particularly in relation to the Muslim army? What can you tell us about snipers, did they exist, how many were there, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: There were plenty of snipers and in fact, it was one of the key defences that the Presidency forces had was snipers and they had them in -- I mean they were sniping at the UN, they were sniping at the Serbs and I've already told you about the anti-sniper team. It was about four people that came to the PTT one day to actually do sniping at their own people in what I call the student accommodation block which was on that corner of the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Earlier, you said there were plenty of -- but were you referring to one army in particular or can you be specific? What can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: The Presidency forces had, as I have said before, they had more people as opposed to heavy weapons. The Serb side had heavy weapons but less people so -- I mean there was an exchange right outside the PTT of ten tonne trucks exchanging weapons which had been taken from Marsal Tito barracks, Viktor Bubanj barracks, you name it they were exchanged so you they had -- the Muslim or Presidency side had plenty of small arms and they had plenty of ammunition and so that's why sniping for them was far, far more efficient than what they didn't have, which was heavy artillery or mortars or tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you tell us about an exchange or a -- plenty of ammunition, that there was passage of ammunition, what can you tell us when this happened and at which location?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: With the -- well the main exchange of ammunition and weapons happened at the PTT building and it happened in June and it was a pre-requirement for the evacuation of Marsal Tito barracks. Marshal Tito barracks, obviously is in the centre of Sarajevo. It was totally surrounded and unless they were actually -- unless the ammunition and the weapons were passed across, then the soldiers inside the barracks would not be allowed to leave. So they had very large trucks loaded with ammunition and weapons which were -- were passed across from the Serbian side to -- well, the in fact, the JNA, they were passed from the JNA to the Muslim or Presidency side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we'll no doubt come back to the question of the Viktor Bubanj barracks but for the time being, I'd like to have a look at the next sequence please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think we should do that after the break. Please keep in mind your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher already to bring the witness in, Mr. Ierace, or would it need so much time or --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. President. I don't think I will be longer than a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I make a proposal as to the procedure that we follow with a view to allowing the Prosecution to efficiently prepare its cross-examination. Mr. President, would it be acceptable if cross-examination tonight only took five or ten minutes so as to clarify with the witness what aspects of his evidence so far are video. A number of times the witness has said, "This is on video. I have video of that." It's not clear to me, having viewed the videotapes whether there is, on the tapes -- whether there are, on the tapes, images to particular aspects of his testimony. With that information from the witness, hopefully overnight and tomorrow, we can locate the relevant segments and then by placing them on a separate tape, play them and proceed from that point. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have two problems. First problem is this one and then the second is the second problem. I'm going to start with the second problem or the other problem. In order to assist the Prosecution with leave -- with the authorisation of Madam Registrar, we gave the original to the Prosecution of the tape and in order to have the same material, and I think that the tape can be brought -- is being brought into the courtroom now, so my second problem is taken care of so if we now give this tape to the technical booth, we will then be able to replay it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the problems is solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, both are resolved because the Prosecution now has in their hands the extracts that we pointed to so there is no point of doing this exercise because the Prosecution has the tape that we were going to tender in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I clarified with Mr. Piletta-Zanin during the break that the tape we have just copied does not have the complete segments. The two tapes which contain BBC interviews are not numbered so it's not possible to determine whether on those two tapes these excerpts come from. The Defence has not taped the whole two or three minutes but bits of the two or three minutes. When I went through the tapes last night and this morning, I made some notes of each segment but that does not assist me to locate two of the segments that we've just seen. That's the problem the Prosecution now has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and would it be solved by just putting a few questions at the end of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That would help, yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not oppose against your suggestion, Mr. Ierace, but let's first now resume the examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Some procedural matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the technical booth, could we now please have the fifth part of this cassette?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, here, we are told about a secret workshop. What can you tell us about what you saw on this tape in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't detect anything on the tape to the effect that it was a secret workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It was said in English, unfortunately, but it was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was said but if they would have said that whatever it was, I mean are we discussing here the comments given by --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, no, my question was to ask the witness about his comments, what Mr. Ierace said that there was no expression "secret workshop" which was clearly used on this tape. Now, perhaps if this is necessary, then we can have it replayed but it was said in English and it was very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I looked at your question. You -- I would say adequately said that we were told about a secret workshop and that's what is said on the video. Yes. At least that's what the voice says. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, in this workshop which was presented as being a secret one, you were able to see a number of elements. Can you tell us if you recognise these elements, perhaps, as being parts of weapons, I don't know, but what did you recognise as being military that can be useful for the Chamber to know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: The workshop that was portrayed in that particular video clip was actually in the basement of the PTT building and those weapons were being remanufactured. There's another part of a video clip that wasn't being shown but it actually shows them manufacturing weapons as well as repairing weapons but part of the clip that you showed only showed them repairing weapons but they were actually manufacturing weapons as well and that was in the basement of the PTT.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how can you be so sure and affirmative of the location of this workshop?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I am absolutely certain and if you want to replay the tape and stop it frame by frame, I can explain exactly why I know it is in the PTT because there are -- in one backdrop they actually show windows, okay, large windows, and that is most definitely the PTT basement and that's where this workshop was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps we can replay this tape later on, but now let us go to another tape and I would like to ask the technical booth to show the next sequence but to show it quickly, to show it before the scene that we are interested in, showing a mortar, I think, but it's a specific weapon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would be grateful if we can fastforward from here until the point of a specific weapon scene. Thank you. Continue, please. Fastforward, please. Stop. Stop. You can continue to play it normally, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Can we now come back to the frame of the scene of the weapon, just before. Yes, thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you an image, first of all, do you appear on this image?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the weapon that you see before you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is located at the -- behind the two people on the right of the image, we can see an opening, what is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That is a protective bunker for people to take cover for incoming fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this type of facility, this mortar and also everything else that we can see with the mortar, is this something that is usual?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, earlier in -- when the video was fastforwarded we saw other weapons. What were they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: They were 122-millimetre Howitzers. There's an important thing about the mortar that you're looking at right now that I should lay some emphasis on to. It is -- it's got weeds growing around its actual base plate, the actual thing where the barrel is going into, you just can't quite see it on the screen. There are weeds growing around it. It hadn't been fired in weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I presume that we are now -- can see the end of this scene, please, normal -- played normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we can stop here. No, just before, thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, here, we see this weapon that is being covered by its cover. Where were its -- by what traces were you able to establish the absence of fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: The fact that the -- around the base plate there are weeds growing which means that it hadn't been fired in weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The base plate, is that the part where we see that the person is extending their left hand?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now ask the very last question which is the following: Since you have checked this position and the others, can you locate where these batteries were?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I handed over a map, I think, to -- plus my diary and a trace which the Court has, if they can give me that map, I can locate it precisely on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of someone and with the leave of Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We told the witness that we would return to him the documents he put at our disposal. These are maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I need the map. Okay. That was Lima 5 -- I'm sorry. That's Lima 5 here, it's located here. That's where that is precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you just zoom in a little bit so that we know. Could you zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is Lima 5 and that is the position of those 120-mil. mortars and the 122-millimetre Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think, there president, that Lima 5 is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Of these maps made, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness points at a circle just south from where it reads Kadino Br. which I understand to be Kadino Brdo and with blue letters Lukavac is written it seems to be the name of a river or a stream. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we now have a look at the tape that follows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They haven't been fired in weeks. You can see the weeds, see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here we are, thank you. No, no, no. The sequence that I'm interested in is the one that begins with the shots that we heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, I noticed that you spoke some words very softly. We couldn't hear that. If there's any comment to be made, you are certainly -- yes, a few words were translated -- at least appear in the transcript. If there's any comment to be made, may I invite you to wait until the sequence is finished.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have taken note of these comments. Thank you. Now, the technical booth, the sequence that starts with shots from a window. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at the end of this sequence, before the close-up of the word airport, we saw a shot which hit the facade of a building; did you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your opinion, what kind of a shot was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It came from a rifle grenade and then there was a 82 millimetre mortar bomb that landed just there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, were you able to hear the comment clearly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear the text on the video clearly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We're told that in this part of Sarajevo, the Serbs were on the defensive. My question is on the basis of your experience, were there several, were there many circumstances when you had such situations? That is to say, there were Serbs who were on the defensive and who were attempting to respond to attacks carried out by the enemy side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, I have that experience. Ilidza is mentioned in the actual -- the video, but Nedzarici was under constant siege and that was right next to the airport. I as part of the second agreement for the concentration of weapons, I negotiated with the local commander in Nedzarici to establish UN observers there but unfortunately, the second agreement was not honoured by the UN. I didn't get the extra observers and so it never happened but Ilidza was definitely under attack a lot and -- because you had -- basically between Nedzarici and Ilidza there was Stup and Stup was held by Croats. So Nedzarici was totally isolated and you had to be very brave to move from Nedzarici to Ilidza just to get the food and water and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. As far as you can remember, what was the extent of the destruction of damage in Nedzarici which is an area you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It was significant and I conducted one meeting there which was involved with putting military observers into Nedzarici. That meeting had to be -- happen at night. In fact I was forced to stay there overnight and on that particular night, Nedzarici took 122-millimetre artillery fire, the shells were landing 20 metres from where I was actually sitting. The shell fragments, the shrapnel was coming through the window into the room I was actually in and on the very same evening, the PTT was shelled by the same 122-millimetre Howitzers. I later found out that those guns were fired by the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the damage was significant. I would like to ask you the same question for the central part of Nedzarici. Was the situation there similar, was it the same?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you explain the extent of this destruction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It was caused by shell fire and mortar bombs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But how do you explain the fact that such shells, whether they were direct artillery shells or indirect artillery shells, how do you explain that they could fall in the centre of the area given that the conflict was usually ongoing along the perimeter of the this area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: The conflict, the direct conflict, you're correct, was actually on the perimeter, I mean that's where the front line was. And Nedzarici was facing in three different directions all at once, against the Croats and against the Muslims. And they were facing the other way which was towards the airport because they were actually attacked by the Presidency forces from that side and on one of the videotapes, you will see two destroyed tanks very clearly, and those tanks were used one night to try and actually infiltrate and capture Nedzarici. But the actual destruction in Nedzarici was very simple because all you need is a map, that's all you need and you just -- as an artillery officer, you just work out bearing whatever and you just fire and that's why the shells were landing in the middle of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By referring to a map, you are saying that the centre was deliberately targeted; is that how I am to take what you said?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to examine an issue and then we will view two other sequences. You mentioned about the steps you took as a negotiator and I think that it is the right moment now to examine what the situation was in relation to General Galic. What can you tell us about General Galic's activities in relation to establishing a peace agreement or in relation to reaching a peace agreement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: When General Sipcic ceased to be the commander of the Sarajevo corps and General Galic took over, I undertook to reach this new agreement. I obviously negotiated with General Galic, I also negotiated directly with Radovan Karadzic and also with Ratko Mladic, the commanding Serb general for the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I'd like to concentrate on the personality of General Galic in relation to his personal willingness to obtain or not to obtain such a peace agreement and I would like to remind you that yesterday, you said that you saw him very frequently, that you saw him very regularly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: He was, to start off with, and I mean that is understandable, he was a little bit reluctant, but he then got orders and instructions, obviously from Pale and Professor Koljevic who was one of the key players in all of this, but he was then very cooperative and he was willing to show me all the positions. Now, I actually went round a lot of the positions that were not under UN observation, I actually met with the commanders there, I observed all their weapons and the cooperation I received from General Galic and the Serbs in general was absolutely excellent. They signed the agreement for the concentration of all heavy weapons first and I then had a fight, a real fight to actually get the other agreement signed by the Presidency side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll return to the -- to the two sequences. I would be grateful if the technical booth could show them now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you are slowly going over the four hours and the Prosecution asked and the Chamber said that the suggestion was to follow it, so...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll make an effort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... For the Prosecution today so you have to finish in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please continue playing the cassette.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, you recognised the last sequence. It's the one you wanted. It has been seen again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as the penultimate sequence is concerned, witness, what can you tell us about what we saw, that is to say, we saw a convoy of white lorries, could you tell us what this represents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That was a French resupply convoy and it was, if you want to bring up the map, it was travelling down this piece of road here -- what we call a Butmir 400.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, witness, if you want to comment, I would like to be able to see the map that we had a look at a minute ago. If you need to mark anything, for example, the part where we can see the airport. Just use the pointer for the moment, please, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: All right. Okay. The road where you saw the lorries is just here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The witness points to a white road which goes along the eastern -- or the southeastern extremity of the airport. Thank you, witness, what happened to these lorries and what was their destination?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: They were a resupply convoy that had come in from Belgrade and they were ambushed by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they to resupply and with what?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: They were resupplying the UN, plus they were also bringing in aid for people in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "people in Sarajevo," which part of Sarajevo are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: All parties. The aid was under the UNHCR as the distribution agency and they distributed it as they could to the different parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please take a black felt-tip and use a cross to mark the point of these attacks.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that this convoy was ambushed by Muslim forces, can you use an arrow to indicate the direction of fire when this convoy was fired at?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you tell us approximately how many lorries there were in the convoy that we saw?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: There were about 20 lorries in it and a point -- a very serious point about this whole ambush was that it was totally deliberate, that the Presidency forces knew that this convoy was coming through and they even had a video camera team there to actually film the ambush on these French -- I've already given evidence to the UN about this particular ambush. I did that in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, can you think of a reason or do you know the reason for which this convoy was attacked?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I have no idea and I have no idea why I was personally attacked 13 times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom and with what?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: By machine-guns, by small arms. The 13 times I talk about are times when I was directly targeted, most of them in broad daylight in an 8-tonne armoured personnel carrier with UN markings on it which -- about two metres high and they all came from the Croats or the Muslims. I was never ever attacked by the Serbs, never ever ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, how can be so sure of this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Well, when you're travelling down the Butmir 400 which is mostly where the attacks happened, and the fire comes from Butmir which was held by the Muslims and you've got bullet strikes on your vehicle and you're standing in the open as I used to, because I -- the crew commander was required to actually stand in the open, and you don't get any bullet strikes from the other side, it's pretty obvious who's actually firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, when you say that you were outside, can you tell us was it a vehicle outside or was it someone who came out of the top part of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, the French armoured personnel carriers had a small turret on the front of them you can see them in the videotapes, whatever,. The crew commander was -- they had a 50 calibre machine-gun there for self-defence but the crew command was required to expose themselves and so there were two hatches at the top of the APC immediately behind the crew commander. It was my practice always to stand up in the hatch and take the same danger that the crew commander was taking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, I apologise for this question but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please keep in mind the time. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten minutes for the Prosecution, is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you understand me perfectly well. I said 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, two questions to conclude: Do you know of any military members who were carrying out their duty and who had less luck than you did? And my second question in relation to the peace agreements which couldn't be signed, what was the reason?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: The peace agreements to deal with your second question first, the peace agreements were signed. They were signed. They were sent to the UN. The airport agreement was honoured by the UN, the first agreement was honoured by the UN. That was the one to initially concentrate the weapons which are shown on this place which is personally signed by Colonel Zivanovic. The second one which was, for me, the most important one which was the concentration of all heavy weapons was not honoured by the UN. Do I know of incidents where UN observers and soldiers were less fortunate than I was because I actually survived the 13 attacks that were made on me and the two death threats that were personally made to me. Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise but I think that the Prosecution can proceed if it considers this to be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, we are almost at the time where we'll stop so you'll get some time for rest but for another few minutes, the counsel for the Prosecution will start asking questions. I expect that they'll not go very much into the substance right away but have some -- need some information from you that are more of a practical nature, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that takes a couple more minutes. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Gray, you gave us last night a map and the tracing paper. I noticed earlier on today you drew another map from your briefcase. They seem to be similar to the one --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. There's nothing to prove that the map concerned was another map, a different map. We don't know which map we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to clarify. The witness is perfectly able to identify if there's a mistake in the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, earlier I noticed you drew a map from your black case and you brought it out and then there was some discussion about whether you should be referred to the map that you'd marked yesterday so you put it back in your briefcase.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was that map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That was a map provided to me by the Defence counsel. It's precisely the same one as the one which has been marked with 1, 2, 3, 4, whatever number we're up to right now. It's exactly the same map. It was just for my own reference and I mean it is -- I mean it's a blow up of what this map is here, which is a map provided from Colonel Zivanovic to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But I thought I saw a map similar to the one you marked pulled out. Could I have a quick look at that. Perhaps it could be passed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, during this time -- well that's not going to help us at this time with the issue of videos is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, is there any markings on that map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there are no markings on it at all it's totally blank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's exactly the same as the one you -- but it's well -- to say a clean copy of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd like to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as far as I can remember, there's only one thing and it's the Defence's stamp and perhaps an exhibit number and that's all. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you wouldn't mind the Chamber would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you insist on seeing it, it's a blank copy of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us about the incident when Lord Carrington went to the Presidency and there were two mortar shells and you've mentioned either yesterday or today or both times that there was some video.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It's on the videotapes which the Defence counsel have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. So some BBC news footage of the incident; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It wasn't that and I was standing right at the front entrance of the Presidency when those mortar bombs landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At this stage I just want to ask you whether it's on the video or not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also today talked about a market shelling; is that somewhere on the video as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... A bomb exploded that's how he explained the event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It probably is. I mean the videotapes, as you are aware, are quite extensive and I think that the market bombing is actually on the videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I've looked at the video and there is a sequence where some people are injured lying on the ground, the footage was apparently shot, it seems, straight after they were injured. I think the benches for the market appear to be concrete or something of that nature?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember when that incident was, approximately? Towards the beginning of when you were there or towards the end --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I believe it was in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. And I think it appears twice in the videotapes, once towards the beginning of the videotape where there's no sound, it seems to be rough footage and then later on as a part of a report by a BBC reporter; does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That would probably be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: There is some repetition in those tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yeah, that's all right. I think twice on the videotapes we see news footages of mosques that have been hit and going by the commentary one was at Butmir and the other one was at Ilidza; does that seem to accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I mean there are mosques also in the old part of the city which were also hit by tank rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. Towards the beginning of one of the tapes, there's some footage of some people in the cemetery and then there's the sound of some weaponry being fired and then we see a -- I think an adult lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- There's some screaming?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: It was a lady, she was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which cemetery was that, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That was in the -- I think the Kosevo one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Near the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now on one of the tapes, the same tape which showed the mortar position and I think field guns in the background?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you were there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When one plays that tape further on do we see the Lukavica headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And at one stage, there was a group of men that walk through a doorway and then there's an examination of a rifle or a machine-gun or something of that nature.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That was at Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That was at Nedzarici. Was that the Nedzarici barracks?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Anywhere on the tape that you remember, do we see the headquarters building at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yes, there is videotapes of that and that's a photo of me at Lukavica barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you have many photos with you there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: No, I should have brought more of them with me. I've been thinking about it the last three days and I actually should have brought a lot more with me. But there is a lot of the video footage will show you Lukavica barracks, it will show you -- I mean I can go through with it -- through it with you. I have no problem with that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just trying to understand what I have seen. At one stage the -- whoever is holding the video camera is following a gentleman making their way through a trench?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: That's right, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you filming or are you in front?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: No I'm in front and that's at Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many floors did the headquarters have?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: In Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: In Lukavica, it had two floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have nothing against the fact that Mr. Ierace is speaking very rapidly but I think that he is now trying to obtain information now which would allow him to work on the cassettes and not start putting specific questions. We're going too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a question you need for preparation this evening or...? So it remains in the technical area rather than to go into the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, to help me to identify the building from the tape. So I should be looking for a building which has ground floor plus --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: In Lukavica, there was only two storey buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ground plus two?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: No. No. Ground plus one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: And the same thing was in Nedzarici as well. It was ground plus one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to help the Prosecution because I can see, I can read the thoughts of the Prosecution, I think, can I ask the witness one question in order to assist the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's -- I think the experience is worth trying but there is a certain risk so --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So to assist myself, Mr. President, perhaps that would assist others too. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it true to say that in Lukavica, apart from the barracks themselves, there were other buildings that could have had more than two floors, as you said? On the rear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yeah, at the back, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the experiment was -- okay, let's not comment on the result of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm grateful to my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you mind if we had a look at the photographs that you've got overnight if they were left with the Court would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, I've only got a couple here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: But I mean -- I should have -- I mean, I've got gazillions of them but I didn't bring them with me. I have no objection to that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have any other notes or anything else that you think might be possibly helpful to us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I think this would be extremely helpful for you and I'm very happy to -- I mean I'm happy to hand over everything that I've got.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What's the particular document that you think might be helpful?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: This is a witness statement for the International War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have a copy.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: You've got a copy. You don't need this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, just the photographs and any other documents that you wouldn't mind us looking at that you think would be helpful if they could be provided to the registry?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY
utterances.text: I'm happy for you to look at anything. I have nothing to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further for tonight, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, so that we are not told that we haven't provided everything, can this witness perhaps show you these three photographs that he has with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have three photographs with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I've just got the three here. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you taken more with you here in The Hague or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are the three photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the only three photographs I've got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we just have a short look at it and I think it's -- if it's only three, Mr. Ierace, then you at least can get an impression that might --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it proves the Defence can't read my mind. They read suspicion when there is none.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, sometimes I read very well but on this occasion, my mind was badly read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would show them to Mr. Ierace and then to Mr. Piletta-Zanin and see whether there is any need to have them copied this evening or that we could wait number tomorrow morning because Madam Registrar has --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, these are three photographs that we have already seen but they seem to be private photographs and that's the reason why I didn't mention them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, we will continue tomorrow. I have to tell you and the parties that, where as I indicated before, that we could not start until after an initial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The information changes every second. I was informed approximately one hour ago that there might be a possibility that we would sit in another courtroom and could then start at quarter past 2.00. Now, it seems to be highly uncertain or even impossible to sit in courtroom 2. Nevertheless, if a courtroom becomes available, we'd like to use the time on from quarter past 2.00 and therefore the parties are directed to keep in close touch with the registry to find out at what time exactly we'll start, preferably at 2.15 but it might be only at 3.15 or 3.30 p.m. And I take it that the registry knows where to reach the parties. Madam Registrar is instructed to keep the detention unit and all the other units involved informed so that no one is unnecessarily suffering from a late start.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one other matter, I see there's no difficulty in the Defence leaving the four tapes with the Prosecution until the commencement of evidence tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would prefer if we followed the same procedure again. I'll speak to Mr. Ierace about it after we have adjourned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... For resolving new problems. Yes, you will -- Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do want the four tapes. It's now time for cross-examination, I've had two of them from -- in terms of having time to look at them -- from end of evidence last night until 9.00 this morning and then the other two tapes since then. I think it's appropriate that we have the four tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that there still has been no opportunity to copy them. Yes. Unfortunately, then, the Prosecution is now preparing for cross-examination so they should be the first ones to have the tapes available but I'm certain, Mr. Ierace, that if I don't know what time at night Mr. Piletta-Zanin asks you to just have a quick look at the tape two or three that you will certainly assist him. Yes. Then that will then be a priority for the Prosecution this evening. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And therefore, am I instructed to hand over those two tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They are, at this moment, where exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have two and the Defence has two. I would be grateful to have the four overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and whenever you need one, you call Mr. Ierace and he's awake as I understand also at 1.30 at night and then he brings it to you. You wanted to say something, Mr. Gray, we have to be quick because the interpreters are really getting exhausted. We'll continue tomorrow but if there is something very urgent please tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I'm just saying to the Prosecution that if they want to see some documents that I hold, then I am happy to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you give full cooperation for disclosure of whatever you have. May I instruct you, especially in view of your cooperative attitude not to speak with anyone, neither Prosecution nor the Defence about your testimony and your testimony is still about to be given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then adjourn until tomorrow in the afternoon, time unknown, courtroom unknown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
